Tiberius. The second Roman emperor, ruling from AD 14 to 37. The stepson of Augustus, he was a brilliant and successful general in his youth, securing the empire's northern frontiers. However, his reign was characterised by growing paranoia, treason trials, and his eventual withdrawal to the island of Capri, leaving the ruthless Praetorian Prefect Sejanus in charge of Rome.

He retreated from Rome in AD 26 to live in a villa on the island of Capri, from which he ruled mostly by correspondence for the rest of his life. He left the day-to-day administration of Rome to Sejanus, the ambitious commander of the Praetorian Guard, before eventually ordering his execution for treason. It was during his reign that Jesus of Nazareth was crucified in the province of Judaea by the governor Pontius Pilate. He was Augustus's stepson through his mother Livia, and was only adopted as heir after the deaths of Augustus's preferred choices, Gaius and Lucius Caesar. Upon his death, the Roman crowds reportedly rejoiced and cried "To the Tiber with Tiberius!"

His stepfather and predecessor was Augustus, who forced him to divorce his beloved wife Vipsania to marry his daughter Julia. His grand-nephew, adopted grandson, and successor was Caligula, who spent time with Tiberius on Capri. The religious figure Jesus was executed in Judaea during his imperial reign. His popular adopted son Germanicus was a successful general whose suspicious death cast a long shadow over his rule.
